scenes.visual: Display the 2D coordinate plane with a smooth paraboloid contour plot representing f(x, y) = x^2 + y^2. Highlight the initial guess point at (2, 2) with a bright dot and label it.

Show the initial vertex at (2, 2) and add two more vertices at (2.1, 2) and (2, 2.1). Connect the three points with lines forming a triangle (simplex). Highlight each vertex with distinct colored dots.
Next to each vertex, display the function value as text: 8 at (2, 2), 8.41 at (2.1, 2), and 8.41 at (2, 2.1). Animate the calculation by showing squares of coordinates and summing them briefly.

Arrange the three vertices vertically on the right side of the screen in ascending order of function values with arrows pointing from the simplex vertices to their sorted positions. Highlight the lowest value vertex (2, 2) in green and the highest two in red.

Calculate and mark the centroid point of the two best vertices (2, 2) and the midpoint of (2.1, 2) and (2, 2.1) as (2.0333, 2.0333). Show the centroid as a distinct dot with a label. Draw dashed lines from these vertices to the centroid.

Animate the reflection of the worst vertex (2.1, 2) across the centroid point (2.0333, 2.0333) to a new reflected point. Show an arrow from the worst vertex through the centroid to the reflected point. Highlight the reflected point with a new colored dot.

scenes.concept: Expansion if reflected point is better
scenes.visual: Show the reflected point moving further away from the centroid along the same line, illustrating expansion. Use an arrow extending beyond the reflected point and highlight the expanded point with a distinct color.

scenes.concept: Contraction if reflected point is worse
scenes.visual: Show the reflected point moving closer to the centroid along the same line, illustrating contraction. Use an arrow pointing from the reflected point towards the centroid and highlight the contracted point with a distinct color.

Animate the simplex shrinking and moving step-by-step towards the origin (0, 0) on the contour plot. Show the vertices approaching the minimum point with the contour lines converging. Highlight the final point at (0, 0) as the minimum.
